what: The tuned-TCP baseline sweep: max_concurrency x parts_in_flight on four link profiles, the untuned default beside it, confirmation runs of the best-tuned point, and contended rows. Raw data: runs.csv (one row per run), objects.csv (one row per batch/object), cycles.csv (one row per process-once), sweep_index.csv (every attempt, refusals included), host_noise.csv. Derived: points.csv, gate.json, charts/ - all regenerated by `python3 benchmarks/egress_baseline.py report --data <this dir> --charts <this dir>/charts`.

host.shared_with: Docker Desktop and its unrelated containers (about ten, other projects), other agents' cargo builds, and the stopped VMs of other projects. Sampled every 30 s into host_noise.csv; not stopped.

lab_vms.why_three: parallel repetitions: the 100 ms profiles are link-bound at 10 Mbit/s, so one VM per repetition cuts wall time without making any one run CPU-bound; every run is still gated on its own calibration
lab_vms.hypervisor: Lima 2.3.0, vz, 6 vCPU, 8 GiB, 40 GiB disk each; vCPUs are not pinned to host cores (vz does not expose that), so 'a pinned core' is not available on this platform
lab_vms.guest: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-142-generic, Docker 29.9.3, Compose v5.7.0
lab_vms.ifb: available (modprobe ifb succeeds), so the middlebox runs exactly as lib/netem.py builds it: policer on the engine-facing ingress hook, upload impairment and bottleneck on the ifb. No egress-shaping substitute was used.

engine_binary.name: vtopctl 0.7.0
engine_binary.source: origin/main 3564edc (engine code unchanged on this branch; the branch adds benchmark Python and docs only)
engine_binary.built_with: rust:latest (rustc 1.99.1) in Docker inside vtop-bench-483a, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, cargo build --release --locked --no-default-features --bin vtopctl; the same file copied to the other two VMs
engine_binary.why_no_default_features: the only default feature is the Kafka source adapter, which links libsasl2; the lab engine image (ubuntu:26.04) has no libsasl2. The file source, batching and the s3_native path measured here do not depend on it.

harness: benchmarks/egress_baseline.py run -> benchmarks/run_benchmark.py, run directly on each VM (python 3.12, PyYAML), runner_mode container, the netem + containerized compose profiles. Engine and store CPU from the containers' cgroup v2 cpu.stat around each run.
workload: one whole 20 MiB JSONL file per batch (whole_file, batch_max_records 1), compression none, sha256, s3_native to the lab MinIO through the middlebox (netem:9200). Backlog max(4, 2 x max_concurrency) objects per run on the shaped profiles, 64 on the clean LAN; the default's width is eight, so 16. Part size 5 MiB on grid points (four parts per object); the default keeps 8 MiB parts and four in flight.

links.lan: the middlebox in the path, no qdisc
links.wan100: netem 100 ms round trip (50 ms each way), no jitter, no loss, tbf 10000 kbit/s at 1.0 BDP (125000 bytes)
links.wan100-loss1: wan100 plus 1% gemodel loss (mean burst two packets) on the upload direction only
links.wan100-policed: netem 100 ms round trip, a 10000 kbit/s policer on the ingress hook, no tbf and no queue
